result.title: LBSNet: Lightweight Brain State Modeling via Learnable Spectral Prototypes for EEG-Based Fatigue Detection
result.summary: EEG-based fatigue detection requires modeling spectral information across bands and its temporal variation. Recent methods combine multi-band modeling with adaptive temporal processing, yet how spectral structure across bands should influence the contribution of each temporal interval remains insufficiently explored. We propose LBSNet, a lightweight network that uses prototype-based brain-state modeling to link local spectral structure with temporal aggregation. LBSNet extracts compact multi-band features through band-specific temporal convolution, shared spatial projections, and cross-band recalibration. Within each window, relative spectral activity is encoded as a normalized descriptor and softly matched to learnable spectral prototypes. Prototype assignments and learned prototype importance jointly determine temporal weights for power aggregation, allowing the spectral pattern of each window to guide its contribution to the prediction. Subject-independent experiments on SEED-VIG and SADT show that LBSNet outperforms seven baselines while maintaining low computational cost. Ablation and visualization analyses support prototype-guided temporal weighting, while the learned prototypes reveal a gradual redistribution of relative cross-band spectral states with increasing fatigue. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/zy0929/LBSNet.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LBSNet，一个轻量 EEG 疲劳检测网络：用频带特定时间卷积、共享空间投影与跨频带重校准提取多频带特征，将窗口内相对频谱活动编码为归一化描述子并与可学习频谱原型软匹配，再由原型分配与原型重要性共同决定时间权重来聚合功率，并在 SEED-VIG、SADT 上做跨被试验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉/多模态推理主线无直接关系，但「可学习原型软匹配 + 原型重要性驱动的时间聚合权重」可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态抽象及各推理片段贡献分配提供方法线索，可供核查。
